parts:
On Sunday, March 17, 2013 8:23:20 PM UTC-4, Peter Li wrote:
I think I've finished implementing RNG for all of the distributions we have so far except for hypergeometric (can't find an effective way to implement a RNG besides actually simulating) and IKJ Corr/Cov (Ben is doing these).

However, I haven't been able to implement effective tests for multi-student t, inv wishart, and wishart, or beta binom. Does anyone have any ideas?

For multivariate student t, the marginals are univariate t, so you can do a chi-squared test of those. For distributions of positive definite matrices, I think we would want to do a test of a scalar function of all the elements in the random variable, such as the determinant. For Wishart and inverse Wishart, see

http://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/34165/expected-value-of-the-log-determinant-of-a-wishart-matrix

Ben
